title: Ask a Bitcoin Maxi...About Psychedelic Medicine?
subtitle: An imagined conversation
text:
The Frontier Psychiatrists has enjoyed doing a series of interviews recently. However, editing those can be a real drag—it’s real people, and they might be offended if I put words in their mouths. Today’s interview is with a fictitious character pulled out of thin air.

As a brief promotional message, remember to buy my books (affiliate links):

Inessential Pharmacology

Adolescent Suicide and Self-Injury

The Hellthread (collected poems)

Why We Skeet (further collected poems)

…and listen to my music on Spotify.

Now, back to our daily articles about whatever I feel like…I watched the Bitcoin Documentary on HBO, so you get this article…

Share

Bitcoin has hit $80,000— an all-time high. For those not familiar with the concept of a bitcoin maxi, it's an abbreviation for bitcoin maximalist. These are individuals who believe so strongly in this one cryptocurrency that are eclipses virtually every other belief that they could have. It is a religious level of fervor and can be obnoxious to be around. These individual's favorite things like an island for bitcoin enthusiast only. Visionary investors are investing in an island on a blockchain:

This is beautifully documented by the inimitable on his Crypto Island limited series, which became Search Engine.But, with Bitcoin hitting new highs, I'm ready to write a little satire for my audience on this fine Sunday!

I'm going to ask and imagine the Bitcoin maxi (BM), a series of questions that have nothing to do with Bitcoin, and see how that imagined conversation goes.

TFPs: What do you think is the most difficult problem facing psychedelic drug development in 2024?

BM: Bro, let's be real—psychedelic drug development in 2024 is hitting roadblocks because the traditional financial system is a total mess. Regulatory hurdles and funding issues are stifling innovation. If the industry embraced Bitcoin, we'd see a decentralized, transparent, and efficient funding model that could bypass these outdated systems. Bitcoin's blockchain could also ensure secure, immutable records for clinical trials, enhancing trust and accelerating approval processes. So, the biggest challenge? Not leveraging Bitcoin's revolutionary potential to transform the entire pharmaceutical landscape.

TFPs: When reviewing the FDA's regulatory guidance as it relates to the development of psychedelic compounds, particularly around the issue of function on blinding in clinical trials for psychedelic medicines, what do you see as the series of ways to meaningfully address the agency’s concerns in a post-Chevron era?

BM: Strap in. THIS is what happens when you connect the dots on how Bitcoin fixes this entire space. You hear me?

Bro, the pharmaceutical industry, including psychedelic trials, is mega bogged down by, like, issues with data manipulation, placebo problems—you know what I mean? Biased reporting. The why should be obvious. The whole system is centralized and relies on old-school flows of capital controlled by big fiat.

Bitcoin is transparent! It has immutable ledgers stored on the blockchain that could decentralize the control of data, ensuring that every inscribed data point—every trial outcome—is permanently and transparently recorded. No more sketchy “reporting.” No more fudged results because some pharma execs want bigger profits on their balance sheets. Everyone could see the truth on chain.

Bitcoin is the only truly decentralized network. Try it with other sh*tcoins. I’m f*cking with you! With Bitcoin, as Satoshi Nakamoto intended, each block, written on the blockchain? We don’t need to sweat it. No Ethereum “founder unlocks,” and no rug-pulls. No one will have the energy—on earth— to “hard fork” this data—just rock-solid, proof-of-work-backed technology.

This matters because clinical trials, especially with psychedelics where blinding and subjective effects are hot topics, need trust. Bitcoin’s ledger is the most secure and trustless system ever created. Trust me when I say there are no “Vitalik” pulling levers or “pre-mined” bags being dumped—Bitcoin just is.

Bitcoin’s decentralized infrastructure empowers researchers globally to share best practices without borders. Fund your lab in El Salvador? Check. Ensure seamless compliance with CE standards in Germany. Check. No wire fees or compliance concerns are hidden deep in a publication supplement. Just pure, unstoppable, peer-to-peer value transfer that respects the researcher and the subject. And think of how this removes bias—researchers aren’t waiting on centralized institutions to greenlight the next steps! Get with the program.

TFPs: How does this exactly address the issue of functional unblinding?

BM: You think a digital stablecoin that some “DAO” controls can beat Bitcoin’s digital scarcity and hard cap of 21 million? Do you want these entities, these “independent” eyes, to be truly impartial? Pay them in Bitcoin. Nothing ensures commitment to transparency and integrity like sound money that cannot be debased. You don’t want any DeFi sketchiness slipping in. When they get paid in Bitcoin, they know it holds value. There’s no better incentive to be unbiased.

TFPs: I didn’t ask about any of that. I wondered about your thoughts about functional unblinding.

BM: Bro, the blockchain is the ultimate blinding assessment. Every transaction is an open ledger entry visible to the entire world. With Bitcoin, all aspects of a trial—funding, data entry, outcomes—could be automatically logged on-chain, turning the trial process into a decentralized, immutable, verified series of transactions—no altcoin smart contract shenanigans, no rug-pulls, pure, verifiable, Bitcoin-backed proof-of-integrity that only grows in value and reliability over time.

TFPs: You are saying the blinding status could be recorded publicly, so we wouldn’t have to wonder if it was successful; we’d know for sure.

BM: I guess that is what I’m saying. From the Genesis block to the marginal block, the whole of history can be inscribed in a way that is impossible to F- with. No one should worry if the trial was conducted this way or that—it’s public! It’s on chain. Say goodbye to wondering.

TFPs: That is a pretty compelling argument.

BM: It’s better than a cartoon ape. Like, get serious. We can’t have the same people who signed off on opiate drugs doing it all over again. Plus, we powered the sink road with bitcoin—I bet those drugs were less dubious than whatever Big Pharma is peddling.

TFPs: In summary?

BM: psychedelics need Bitcoin. The rest? Sh*t. Only Bitcoin has the hash power, decentralized global network, and unbreakable integrity to transform the space, bro. Only Bitcoin.

TFPs: Thanks for joining us, I guess.

BM: Buy the dip.

TFPs: Thanks, I guess.

Editor's note: I do not hold a single Bitcoin or a single satoshi. I have no bitcoin to my name. The above is for the purpose of humor only, not for personal enrichment other than suggesting you subscribe to the newsletter.
